recommendation.status: Azure F0 resource provisioned for feasibility; production quality and thresholds remain unvalidated
recommendation.reason: Supports scripted Spanish pronunciation assessment and has usage-based pricing without a monthly minimum at the verified retail rate. Existing recorder + backend request can avoid a new native SDK/build.
recommendation.acceptance_gate: Validate real short Spanish clips against human judgments before using a score to determine learner success. If accuracy is inadequate, compare another dedicated scorer or explicitly revisit scope; never label plain transcription as a pronunciation check.

distinction.speech_to_text: Recognizes the words in speech. Matching its transcript alone is insufficient evidence of correct pronunciation.
distinction.pronunciation_assessment: Analyzes recorded speech against known reference text and returns acoustic pronunciation scores/error information. The result is a model estimate, not certainty.
distinction.synthesis: César/ElevenLabs produces the reference voice; a pronunciation assessment provider evaluates the learner. These are separate jobs and budgets.

providers.name: Azure Speech
providers.scripted_single_word: Reference text can be a word, sentence or paragraph; real reliability on Hola/Sí/No is not established by documentation.
providers.metrics: Accuracy and word-level results, completeness and miscue information. Do not use native-like speed/fluency as a beginner pass requirement.
limitations: Spanish prosody scoring is unavailable; documented prosody is en-US only.
For Spanish, phoneme scores may exist without phoneme names; do not promise an IPA diagnosis or generated exact-sound correction.
The REST short-audio pronunciation request is limited to30seconds; use short scripted requests.
REST input WAV PCM16kHz mono or supported OGG Opus; current Expo preset requires format verification/conversion.

pricing.free_tier: F0:5 standard real-time audio hours/month, subject to active subscription/quota. Pronunciation baseline is charged as standard STT; verify actual F0 resource access during setup.
pricing.billing: One-second increments; rate is for speech processing only, before tax/hosting/conversion/network.
pricing.enhanced_prosody: Not required for Spanish and not included in the estimate.

providers.name: Speechace
providers.fit: Dedicated word/text scoring API; Score Word supports Spanish and accepts m4a among other formats.

pricing.trial: Free trial advertised; do not infer trial credit amount/duration or eligibility.

providers.tradeoff: Simpler intake for Expo m4a, but a fixed monthly plan is less attractive for a small pilot.

pricing.qualification: Displayed price-page rates; Spanish-specific product/rate must be confirmed before selecting. Prepay plans start at500USD and are not proposed.

cost_examples.assumptions: Paid Azure standard rate1USD/audio-hour, exactly5 billed seconds per attempt, one request per attempt, before F0 allowance and tax/hosting/conversion costs. Silence within submitted audio counts toward duration; retries increase calls.
cost_examples.f0_idealized_capacity: 5hours=18000seconds, about3600 five-second attempts, if all allowance is available. This is a capacity illustration, not an SLA or an allowance automatically applied to a paid tier.

flow: Expo records a short utterance using the existing audio capability.
Authenticated backend receives exerciseId and audio, looks up the approved expected text/locale and applies duration/size/attempt limits.
Backend validates/normalizes codec and converts to supported mono PCM WAV when required; credentials remain server-side.
Backend submits one scripted assessment request, maps word/coverage results to the calibrated learner outcome, and returns concise Hebrew feedback.
Temporary audio is discarded after request processing; retain only minimal assessment/progress metadata if jointly selected.
integration_plan.expo: expo-audio is included in Expo Go; an HTTP/backend approach does not inherently require a native Azure SDK. End-to-end success remains untested; preserve stage04 native-build deferral.
integration_plan.audio_format: Current App.tsx uses RecordingPresets.HIGH_QUALITY. Official current docs describe m4a AAC44100Hz stereo. Verify the installed preset/device file and choose recording options or backend conversion during the spike, without upgrading Expo.
integration_plan.api_suggestion: One small assessment endpoint behind the existing mandatory identity plan, not a separate large backend. Transport/route/auth details belong to stages03/05.
staging: Stage02: source/price research, small feasibility decision, generic feedback-state specification.
Stages03/05: minimal assessment contract and one server-side provider adapter/endpoint after feasibility review.
Stage06: wire recording, assessment, retry, help and progress into the shared speaking component.
No native build now; no full service provisioning or purchase in this research step.

candidate_flow: See the familiar phrase/task and optionally hear the model.

feasibility_test.scope: A small smoke test of about20–30 short clips is a feasibility screen, not statistical validation.
cases: Understandable Spanish spoken with an Israeli accent, including slow beginner speech.
Deliberately wrong word, e.g. Gracias when Hola is expected.
Missing one word from Buenos días.
Clearly distorted target pronunciation, labelled by a proficient Spanish listener.
Silence, background noise, clipped audio and low volume.
Several repetitions of the same recording to check score stability.
evidence_to_collect: Human label and reason, kept separate from provider score.
Recognized words/coverage, word accuracy, assessment availability and raw provider error types.
False rejection of understandable speech and false acceptance of wrong/distorted speech.
Request duration, end-to-end latency, billed audio duration and request count.
Actual iPhone/Expo format and backend conversion result.
feasibility_test.go_no_go: Review disagreements jointly. If no threshold reliably separates acceptable from clearly wrong speech in the short examples, do not make the model an authoritative pass/fail gate. Compare Speechace using the same consented clips and revisit the implementation choice.
feasibility_test.synthetic_reference: Approved César Buenos días may be a technical sanity sample only; it cannot stand in for human beginner/accent validation.
feasibility_test.budget: Start F0, one provider call per submitted clip, small bounded batch, no synthesis, no automatic paid upgrade.
feasibility_test.interim_observation: Reported distortion gets aggregate90.4/word84/ErrorType None but unnamed phoneme scores44/45; do not adopt aggregate-only pass/fail or diagnose a named Spanish sound.

privacy.provider_statement: Microsoft documents no retention/storage of submitted pronunciation-assessment data. Our own backend/log/temp-file behavior still needs implementation and verification.
privacy.product_change: Previously local-only recordings now need temporary cloud processing for assessment. Explain this at recording; account/sign-in and minimal retention rules remain.
privacy.not_selected: Persistent cloud audio archive, voice identity recognition, voice cloning or public sharing.
